result.title: Regularized Score Centering
result.summary: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update. Our gradient diagnostics show less extreme gradients with SC than with importance sampling (IS), but SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. To limit this policy mismatch, we introduce Regularized Score Centering (RSC), which adds a reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) penalty to encourage the learner's next-token distribution to stay close to the behavior policy's next-token distribution. RSC works with or without truncated importance sampling (TIS), which caps token importance weights. Our theoretical analysis supports this approach, showing that KL regularization improves convergence guarantees. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts models on mathematical reasoning and agentic tasks, including online shopping, tool use, games, and fully asynchronous software engineering. RSC with TIS substantially improves sample efficiency across all agentic benchmarks, attaining higher training rewards with the same number of sampled responses. In final evaluations, it achieves top performance across all six agentic tasks, improving by 14.3% on AppWorld and reaching 9.9 times the strongest baseline's score on BabyAI.

AI.brief_summary: 针对异步强化学习中旧策略数据与训练/推理数值不一致带来的不稳定，论文先诊断 score centering（SC）的梯度行为，再提出加入反向 KL 约束使学习器下一 token 分布贴近行为策略的 Regularized Score Centering（RSC），并给出收敛性分析与多类 agentic 任务实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于纯文本 RL 训练稳定性工作，但「用反向 KL 限制学习器偏离产生数据的策略」这一线索可供核查：在异步、长轨迹的 latent/推理状态训练中，如何约束陈旧 rollout 与当前策略的偏差可能有借鉴价值。
